newsitem.title: GERMANY: Analyst sees high mill earnings in CR stainless.
newsitem.headline: Analyst sees high mill earnings in CR stainless.

text.p: Rising demand for cold-rolled (CR) flat stainless steel products and better mill capacity utilisation could secure producers higher earnings up to 2002, analyst Heinz Pariser said.
Heavy investements in new capacity in 1994-95 had been absorbed and raw materials should get cheaper, especially nickel, after the year 2000, when new supply should have arrived, he said.
Pariser forecast global consumption of flat products, which represent two-thirds of the stainless steel market, at 8.39 million tonnes in 1998 and at 10.35 million in 2002 from 7.42 million in 1996.
Pariser, who runs an alloy metal & steel market research bureau in Xanten, Germany, was addressing a conference here.
Stainless steel accounts for two-thirds of nickel use.
Pariser pegged CR capacity in 1998 at 9.56 million in 1998 and 11.56 million in 2002 from 8.67 million in 1996, above consumption.
But demand shifts, especially to Asia, meant producers could make better selective use of capacity, he said.
Overall capacity utilisation should rise to 88 percent in 1998 and 90 percent in 2002 from 85 percent in 1996, below which producers were incurring losses.
Pariser said Asian demand growth, for example for cutlery and holloware, would by far outperform that in Europe, the United States and Japan.
He put the compound annual 1996-2002 growth rate in CR consumption in Asia at 9.4 percent, at 6.2 percent in the U.S., at 3.4 percent in West Europe and at 2.4 percent in Japan.
While 1996 producer profits varied immensely, he believed prudent producers should be able to achieve good profitability in stainless in the years to come.
